answers.text: I'm finishing BA Economics at a government college in Jodhpur. I run the 800 metres and won silver at the state meet in 2024. Last year I captained our college team and organised daily 6 a.m. training for 18 athletes. For a term paper I studied onion prices at the local mandi over 18 months using public data. I want an MBA because sports taught me discipline, and economics gave me theory. I'd like the practical side of running an organisation.
I think the question assumes that sport is a hobby. At state level it needs planning, budgeting for travel and recovery, and long-term goals. I consider it as serious as an internship.
Sports has taught me a great deal about leadership, grit and teamwork. I believe those learnings are applicable everywhere and that I will bring a winning mindset to any organisation.
I won gold at the national meet in 2024, which is what really changed my confidence. The silver was only the state one before that.
Quick question, what do you think about the new cricket league auction? My friends and I were discussing that yesterday. I felt some of the prices were not justified.
